dublinCore.dc:title: 118 S4261 IS: Educator Down Payment Assistance Act of 2024

form.current-chamber: IN THE SENATE OF THE UNITED STATES

action.action-desc: Mr. Heinrich introduced the following bill; which was read twice and referred to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs

form.official-title: To direct the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development to award grants to provide financial assistance to certain educators to make down payments on certain homes, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Educator Down Payment Assistance Act of 2024.

paragraph.text: The term eligible dwelling means a residential property with—

subparagraph.text: not more than 4 dwelling units;
an apartment;
a condominium; or
a manufactured dwelling unit.

paragraph.text: The term eligible educator means a public elementary or secondary school teacher, principal, paraprofessional, school leader, or other staff who—

subparagraph.text: is a first-time homebuyer;
has served in their position or another position in the educational system for not fewer than a total of 3 years (without regard to whether such years were consecutive);
has a qualifying income; and
is in good standing.
a unit of local government;
a State housing finance agency; or
a local educational agency.

paragraph.text: The term eligible residential mortgage loan means a residential mortgage loan that—

subparagraph.text: meets the underwriting requirements and dollar amount limitations for acquisition by the Federal National Mortgage Association or the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation;
is made, insured, or guaranteed under title II of the National Housing Act (12 U.S.C. 1707 et seq.) or title V of the Housing Act of 1949 (42 U.S.C. 1471 et seq.);
is made, insured, or guaranteed under title VIII of the Native American Housing Assistance and Self-Determination Act of 1996 (25 U.S.C. 4221 et seq.);
is a qualified mortgage, as defined in section 129C(b)(2) of the Truth in Lending Act (15 U.S.C. 1639c(b)(2)); or
is guaranteed under section 184 of the Housing and Community Development Act of 1992 (12 U.S.C. 1715z–13a).
military deployment;
divorce;
death of an eligible educator or spouse; and
other similar unforeseen events as determined by the Secretary.

paragraph.text: The terms elementary school, local educational agency, other staff, secondary school, and Secretary have the meanings given such terms in section 8101 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act of 1965 (20 U.S.C. 7801).

The term first-time homebuyer has the meaning given the term in section 92.2 of title 24, Code of Federal Regulations (as in effect on the date of the enactment of this Act), except that any reference in such section to the American Dream Downpayment Initiative shall be deemed to be a reference to the grant program established under this section.

The term good standing means that, with respect to an eligible educator and during the 3-year period beginning on the date on which the educator submits an application under section 3(b), such educator has not received disciplinary action from the local educational agency that serves the school at which such educator works as an educator.

subparagraph.text: an income that is not greater than 120 percent of the area median income in which the eligible dwelling to be purchased is located; and
if the Secretary determines that the area described in subparagraph (A) is a high-cost area, an income that is not greater than 180 percent of the median income of such area.

paragraph.text: The term Secretary means the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development.

section.header: First-time homebuyer down payment assistance program

subsection.text: The Secretary of Housing and Urban Development shall award grants, on a competitive basis, to eligible entities to provide financial assistance to eligible educators in accordance with subsection (d).

An eligible entity seeking a grant under this section shall submit to the Secretary an application in such form, at such time, and containing such information as the Secretary determines appropriate, including an assurance that such entity will use an existing, or establish a new, down payment assistance program to provide financial assistance to eligible educators.

In the case of a geographic area that is served by an eligible entity that is a unit of local government and an eligible entity that is a local educational agency, the Secretary may only award a grant to 1 such entity in such geographic area.

subsection.header: Use of amounts To provide financial assistance

paragraph.text: An eligible entity that receives a grant under subsection (a) shall use such grant funds to provide financial assistance to eligible educators.

An eligible educator seeking a financial assistance under this subsection shall submit to the eligible entity an application in such form, at such time, and containing such information as the eligible entity determines appropriate, including an assurance that such educator will—

subparagraph.text: complete the housing counseling required under paragraph (8); and
use an eligible residential mortgage loan to purchase an eligible dwelling.

paragraph.text: An eligible educator who receives financial assistance under this subsection shall use such financial assistance to pay, with respect to the purchase of an eligible dwelling using an eligible residential mortgage loan, for—

subparagraph.text: direct down payment costs associated with such purchase;
closing costs associated with such purchase; and
costs related to reducing the rates of interest on such eligible residential mortgage loan associated with such purchase.
Except as provided under subparagraph (B), the amount of financial assistance awarded to an eligible educator under this subsection may not be greater than $25,000.

In the case of an eligible educator purchasing an eligible dwelling that is located in an area described in section 305(a)(2) of the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation Act (12 U.S.C. 1454(a)(2)), the amount of financial assistance awarded to an eligible educator under this subsection may be greater than $25,000.

paragraph.text: An eligible educator may only receive financial assistance under this subsection 1 time.

An eligible entity may award financial assistance under this subsection to an eligible educator who is receiving funds from other sources, including other State, Federal, local, private, public, and nonprofit sources, for the purpose of purchasing an eligible dwelling.

subparagraph.text: An eligible educator who is awarded financial assistance under this subsection shall use the eligible dwelling purchased using such financial assistance as a primary residence for a period of not fewer than 3 years beginning on the date on which the eligible educator receives financial assistance under this subsection.

clause.text: An eligible educator who does not comply with the requirement under subparagraph (A) shall return to the eligible entity the total amount of the financial assistance awarded to such educator under this subsection.

Such funds shall be returned in accordance with clause (i) not later than 1 year after such educator ceases to use such dwelling as a primary residence in violation of the requirement under subparagraph (A).
An eligible educator who does not comply with the requirement under subparagraph (A) due to an emergency event shall not be required to return financial assistance under clause (i).

subparagraph.text: An eligible educator who is awarded financial assistance under this subsection shall be required by the Secretary to continue in their role as a public elementary or secondary school teacher, principal, paraprofessional, school leader, or other staff for not less than 3 years after the date on which the eligible educator is awarded financial assistance.
Subparagraph (A) shall not apply if an eligible educator is a military spouse, as defined in section 45AA(d)(1) of the Internal Revenue Code of 1986.

subsection.text: The Secretary shall submit to Congress an annual report that includes include a breakdown of financial assistance provided under this section, by demographic breakdown, mean income, and mean purchase price.
There are authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $30,000,000 for each of fiscal years 2025 through 2030.
